newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI Australia IPO sees strong demand.
newsitem.headline: ICI Australia IPO sees strong demand.

text.p: The offer of ICI Australia Ltd shares being sold by its U.K. parent, Imperial Chemical Industries Plc, has brought a good response from retail subscribers, an underwriter of the issue said on Wednesday.

"There has been strong retail demand according to indications we have from the (share) registry," Wayne Kent, a spokesman from Macquarie Underwriting, one of the joint underwriters of the issue told Reuters.
ICI Plc announced plans to sell its 62.4 percent stake in ICI Australia last month through a global share offer and a share buy-back by ICI Australia Australia.
The retail offer closed at 10 a.m (0000 GMT) today while the institutional offer closes on July 11.
Kent said he could not comment on the progress of the institutional offer but brokers said there was also expected to be strong interest in the offer from local and offshore institutions.
The retail offer is capped at A$12.40, valuing ICI Australia at A$3.7 billion. Retail investors are guaranteed a 40 cent discount to the final share price.
ICI Australia shares have traded consistently above the A$12.40 price since the offer was announced, helping to make the offer attractive to retail investors.
The final price of the offer will be set after considering institutional bids and will be announced on July 12.
In late June, ICI Australia's shareholders approved a plan to buy back up to 10 percent of the company's shares from ICI plc, which could cost as much as A$360 million.
At 1.10 p.m (0310 GMT), ICI Australia shares were 19 cents weaker at A$12.61.
